definitions.explanation: Leaves that have fallen from trees, especially in autumn. A word closely associated with the autumn season in Japanese culture and literature.

examples.japanese: ⟦{公園|こうえん}→公園：00581_kouen⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{道|みち}→道：00505_michi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{落|お}ち{葉|ば}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{埋|う}め→埋める：01901_umeru⟧⟦{尽|つ}くされている→尽くす：02077_tsukusu⟧。
examples.english: The park path is completely covered with fallen leaves.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもたち⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{色|いろ}とりどり→色とりどり：10404_irotoridori⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{落|お}ち{葉|ば}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{拾|ひろ}い{集|あつ}めて、{押|お}し{葉|ば}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{工作|こうさく}→工作：12437_kousaku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{楽|たの}しんでいた→楽しむ：01203_tanoshimu⟧。
examples.english: The children were gathering colorful fallen leaves and enjoying making pressed-leaf crafts.

notes:
USAGE:
{落|お}ち{葉|ば} is a seasonal word (⟦{季語|きご}→季語：09561_kigo⟧) associated with autumn. It evokes the beauty and melancholy of the autumn season and appears frequently in poetry and literature.

{落|お}ち{葉|ば}⟦{焚|た}き→焚く：02285_taku⟧ (burning fallen leaves) was once a common autumn activity in Japan, though it is now restricted in many areas due to environmental regulations.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {落|お}ち{葉|ば}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{掃|は}く→掃く：04260_haku⟧ (sweep fallen leaves)
- {落|お}ち{葉|ば}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{拾|ひろ}う→拾う：00845_hirou⟧ (pick up fallen leaves)
- {落|お}ち{葉|ば}⟦{焚|た}き→焚く：02285_taku⟧ (burning fallen leaves)
- {落|お}ち{葉|ば}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{舞|ま}う→舞う：04573_mau⟧ (fallen leaves dance in the air)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{枯|か}れ{葉|は}→枯れ葉：20386_kareha⟧: dried/withered leaf (emphasizes the dry, dead state)
- ⟦{紅葉|こうよう}→紅葉：04151_kouyou⟧: autumn foliage (leaves still on the tree, or the act of changing color)
- ⟦{落葉樹|らくようじゅ}→落葉樹：04961_rakuyouju⟧: deciduous tree
